_source: sequential eval run 6 (docs/evals/2026-08-04-run-6.md), 5/5 cases, 19/19 checks; parallel runs excluded — API contention inflates per-case durations 2-6x (run 3 finding)
_policy: hard ceilings: run-evals.sh fails a case that exceeds duration, attributed tokens, or billed USD, and fails closed when cost evidence is missing. Parallel runs skip only duration because contention makes it incomparable. Ceiling changes require reviewed evidence from an accepted sequential run.
_metrics: Three ceilings, because each catches a regression the others miss. max_seconds is wall clock. max_usd is the CLI's own total_cost_usd — the real cost, and the only one that catches a model-mix regression (a sonnet -> opus re-tier keeps token counts flat and triples the bill). max_tokens is attributed.total.tokens — a work-volume proxy that is invariant to pricing, which max_usd is not — so on a max_usd breach, check the rate-table reconciliation in <case>.cost.json before assuming a regression. The one dated price risk is now RETIRED: Sonnet 5's introductory rate expiring 2026-08-31 does not affect these ceilings, because billing was shown to be at list price already (see model-rates.json's _source for the arithmetic). TIE-BREAK (2026-08-06): max_usd is the cost metric of record. When the ceilings disagree, dollars win — token totals are >99% cache reads (they measure conversation shape, not spend) and wall clock measures the experience, not the bill (run 6: security-engineer was 53% of policy's wall clock and a sixth of its bill). Seconds and tokens remain as ceilings because each catches regressions dollars miss; they just do not outvote it. Bimodal exception unchanged: check _bimodal_cases before calling any policy/action number a regression.
_tokens_caveat: Run 6 measured token totals as >99% cache-read tokens in all five cases (e.g. n-plus-one: 3,666,860 cache of 3,669,451 total). Cache reads bill at 0.1x input, so max_tokens tracks context volume x turns far more than it tracks spend. Read it as a work-volume signal and let max_usd speak for cost.
_bimodal_cases: `policy` and `action` each run two ways: the coordinator fast path takes the case (fewer stages, much cheaper) or it delegates. Run 5 delegated `policy` (994s) and fast-pathed `action` (420s); run 6 did the exact opposite (`policy` 381s undelegated, `action` 1217s across 4 agents); a targeted 2026-08-05 run caught `policy` delegating again (1560s, $7.18, 4 agents). The spread on one case is 3.3x in dollars, so BOTH cases' ceilings are seeded to cover the delegating mode — an undelegated run then reads comfortably inside them, and the agent list in <case>.cost.json is what tells you which mode ran. Check that list before treating any REGRESSED reading on these two as a regression.
_opt_in: Five cases are registered but excluded from the default sweep (OPT_IN_CASES in run-evals.sh) because each is expensive and only needs re-measuring when coordinator/team-memory behaviour changes — the coordinator_hash gate below is the trigger that says when. `feature`: the only case guaranteed to delegate, seeded from its first run (2026-08-04): 1456s, $6.55, 11.2M tokens — 5/6 checks; the miss was the stage-budget assertion, later shown in run 7 to be a stale check reading a real pass as a fail (docs/evals/2026-08-06-run-7.md finding 3), so its true score is 6/6. `feature-adaptive`: same Tag --api ceilings as `feature` until a billed Adaptive run reseeds. `feature-resume`: same Tag --api floor as `feature`, planted with a running close.md and a completed database-developer stage, until a billed pin. `teach` and `teach-delivery`: run 7's split hypothesis (docs/evals/2026-08-06-run-7-scope.md) — teach/override held from run 7; harvest held too as of v1.41.0 (docs/evals/2026-08-06-run-7.md second addendum), once the requirement moved into the shared Interface block all 9 commands read.

policy.basis: both modes now measured: 381s undelegated (run 6) and 1560s delegating across 4 agents (2026-08-05). Seeded to cover the delegating mode, so an undelegated run reads far inside it — the agent list in <case>.cost.json, not this ceiling, is what tells you which mode ran
policy.tokens_basis: delegating run: 11,362,290 + ~28%. The undelegated run was 4,371,934
policy.usd_basis: delegating run: $7.18 billed + ~25%. The undelegated run was $2.19 — a 3.3x spread between modes on the same case, which is why the mode matters more than the ceiling

action.basis: run 6: 1217s across 4 agents (qa-engineer, main, tech-lead, backend-developer) + headroom. The previous 600s came from run 5's 420s fast-path run, and its basis note predicted exactly this: 'if the fast path stops taking it, this reads REGRESSED the first time it delegates again — that is the intended signal'. The signal fired as designed; the ceiling now covers the delegating mode

action.usd_basis: run 6: $5.16 billed + ~30%. 41% of the whole run's $12.50

teach-delivery.basis: v1.41.0 re-run (2026-08-07, docs/evals/2026-08-06-run-7.md second addendum): 939s, main thread + 4 specialists (database-developer, backend-developer, qa-engineer, tech-lead) + ~30%, capped below EVAL_TIMEOUT=1200s — the +30% math alone would land at 1220s, past the harness's own hard kill, which cannot be a valid ceiling since no run can ever measure above 1200s without timing out first (this same defect existed at 1250s before this reseed, inherited rather than introduced). This is the first CLEAN measurement of the real fix — harvest requirement moved into the shared Interface block all 9 commands carry, confirmed by reading docs/team/stack.md and docs/delivery/donation/log.md directly, not by the check's word. Supersedes run 7's basis, which measured a run where harvest was structurally unable to fire

coordinator_hash.note: Pinned after 3.3 workplace Interface. No billed pin. Do not raise ceilings.

waivers.reason: Security and control-plane hardening: typed shell-free verification, explicit user approval for learned rules, kernel-owned ready/claim concurrency with path locks, runtime budgets/recovery, and trace redaction/retention. Covered by kernel/console units, guardrails, and deterministic trace replay. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.

Runtime stage approvals add one pre-dispatch gate without changing feature construction: declared categories are profile-validated, pending lanes are excluded from ready, claim fails before user approval, subagent self-grants and direct kernel-state writes are blocked, and durable provenance is covered by kernel units plus hook integration tests. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.

Kernel-enforced runtime stage budgets change the shared dispatch interface but not feature construction: every lane receives snapshotted limits, Claude meters pre-tool and completion usage, other runtimes submit the same five-dimensional receipt, and missing telemetry or overages stop the lane durably. Covered by kernel units, hook integration, guardrails, and deterministic trace replay. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.

Criterion-linked verification changes the reporting contract but not feature construction: plans assign stable criterion IDs, every passing runner record covers exactly one declared criterion, incomplete coverage fails closed, and only a durable main-thread user decision may waive evidence. Covered by kernel units, hook integration, guardrails, and generated-target checks. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.

Durable human checkpoints change interruption recovery but not feature construction: the main thread stores the exact prompt before asking, pending state pauses only its lane, user answers requeue or stop deterministically, and resumes never reconstruct or repeat decisions. Covered by kernel units, CLI tests, hook integration, orchestration ratchets, and generated-target checks. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.

Unproductive-loop detection adds a pre-tool stop boundary without changing feature construction: claimed specialists are stopped before completing a third exact one-to-four-step tool cycle, raw inputs are represented only by SHA-256 digests, and unchanged retries are prohibited. Covered by kernel units, hook integration, guardrail ratchets, and generated-target checks. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.

Auditable retry transitions tighten the shared orchestration contract without changing feature construction: one main-thread retry request requeues for a fresh claim, stable event IDs make duplicate feedback idempotent, reports require a claimed measured lane, and a second distinct failure stops with consistent stage status. Covered by kernel units, CLI tests, hook integration, orchestration ratchets, and generated-target checks. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.

Interruption recovery tightens resumed dispatch without changing feature construction: confirmed dead claims freeze at last observed activity, unavailable completion metrics remain explicit, continue requeues through a fresh claim without consuming the retry, and stop remains terminal. Covered by kernel units, CLI tests, policy integration, orchestration ratchets, and generated-target checks. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.

Stage-owned PR and CI feedback tightens repair routing without changing feature construction: exact declared check names and longest owned-path matches select the owner, unmatched events block dispatch for main-thread assignment, duplicate events are idempotent, and one passing repair resolves the grouped feedback wave. Covered by kernel and console units, policy integration, orchestration ratchets, generated-target checks, and the existing eval suite. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.

Canonical orchestration generation changes ownership of existing prompt text without changing feature construction: nine commands and the direct coordinator now materialize one byte-identical lifecycle contract, CI rejects missing or unexpected carriers and hand-edited drift, and coordinator-only board, brief, and adaptive rules remain explicit. Covered by dedicated sync units, orchestration ratchets, inventory hashing, and generated-target checks. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.

Delivery observability adds an integrity check at resume and closure without changing feature construction: every persisted mutation emits a schema-versioned correlated event, deterministic derived views are checked against authoritative kernel state, unhealthy traces stop dispatch, and legacy state is not backfilled with invented history. Covered by observability and kernel units, canonical-sync ratchets, guardrails, and generated-target checks. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.

Outcome benchmark enforcement adds a verification gate without changing feature construction: declared performance criteria require repeated read-only baseline/candidate captures, behavioral equivalence, objective-specific query and latency thresholds, and a source-bound receipt that the kernel re-verifies. Covered by benchmark and kernel units, orchestration ratchets, guardrails, enforcement-map checks, and generated-target checks. No billed feature run was authorized; ceilings were not raised.
